presentation.label: TAPE SATURATION
presentation.summary: JClones TapeHead on the DSP: a small tape-style saturator with drive, trim and three tone colours.
presentation.overview: TapeHead runs the input through a two-state recursion whose corner frequency COLOR sets, drives both states into cubic smoothstep curves and adds a clipped feedback term. Low DRIVE gives gentle rounding and a slight tilt; high DRIVE flattens peaks and thickens the low end. It is a buffer-free insert, so it runs on FX1 or FX2 of every track.
highlights: Port of JClones_TapeHead.jsfx, within 4.7e-4 of the float reference in a native render
DRIVE and TRIM as continuous 0-127 knobs over the JSFX ranges
COLOR: NORM, MED and BRGT corners at 2100, 3680 and 5000 Hz
No buffers: FX1 or FX2 on any track, 288 cycles/sample static
usage: Assign TAPEHEAD in FUNC + FX2 (or FX1) SETUP with LEVEL and YES. Defaults match the JSFX: DRIVE 36, TRIM 18 (-3 dB), COLOR NORM.
Raise DRIVE for more saturation; lower TRIM (towards 0) to bring the level back up, raise it to attenuate down to -21 dB.
Use COLOR for brightness: MED and BRGT move the recursion's corner up and let more top end through the saturator.

controls.name: DRIVE
controls.doc: Tape drive. 0-127 maps to the JSFX drive 1-10 (gain 0.8x to 8x into the curves); 36 is about the JSFX default 3.5.

controls.name: TRIM
controls.doc: Output trim. 0 is 0 dB, 127 is -21 dB; 18 is the JSFX default -3 dB. Higher values are quieter.

controls.name: COLOR
controls.doc: Corner frequency of the recursion: NORM 2100 Hz, MED 3680 Hz, BRGT 5000 Hz.

limitations: The JSFX Clip switch is not exposed. Clip is always on (the JSFX default), because Q1.23 cannot carry the unclipped mode.
Corner frequencies assume 44.1 kHz, the rate every Octamod effect assumes.

This revision changes the sound of the octabam build heard on 12 Sep 2026: three defects were fixed (see TESTING.md). The OCTABAM2 test image of this revision was flashed and listened to on 2 Oct 2026; it has not been stress-tested.
Effect ID 0x1f, priority 17 and layout letter 4 were checked free against the eleven Octamod modules only.
Hardware operation and parameter locks are author-reported; the Octatrack model, duration and maximum tested load were not specified.
As with other modules, a crowded selection can exceed DSP or menu space and is refused by the builder.
Analog BD currently requires stock DSP effects; the builder refuses TapeHead together with Analog BD.

storage.label: DSP program
storage.display: 422 words P, 31 words X per instance, no buffer
storage.conditions: Composed build report (both payloads place 422 words in the donor region). State and scratch use 31 words of the instance's own r7 block; no allocator buffer, no Y memory. SPRING REV: 1,063 words plus the 16,384-word FX2 instance buffer.

processing.label: DSP estimate
processing.conditions: tools/build/cycle_count.py static word count, the same at every setting. benchmark.py, executed instructions: 274/sample for one instance (SPRING REV 262); four per core worst 18,000 per 16-sample block (SPRING REV 20,376). Not a hardware load figure.

impact.conditions: One active instance at any setting (no stage is skipped, COLOR only swaps constants); the static count covers the worst case.

cpu.rationale: No ColdFire code: the module is a DSP insert with a cloned menu descriptor. The ColdFire only forwards three page-1 parameter values, as for any effect.

dsp.rationale: 295 cycles/sample per instance by the static counter. benchmark.py: one instance executes 5% more than stock SPRING REV (4,383 vs 4,186 instructions per block); four per core peak 12% lower (18,000 vs 20,376) because Spring's costlier types and splits are absent.

memory.rationale: 422 words of DSP program per payload and 31 words of state in each instance's existing r7 block. No allocator buffer, tables or Y memory, where SPRING REV takes 1,063 words and a 16,384-word instance buffer.

tests.summary: Native render matches the JClones reference within 5.4e-4 at the JSFX's own level, with the Octatrack's AMP VOL gain staging compensated (+12 dB in, -12 dB out). Both-core modulated/split benchmark, static cycle accounting and exact memory inventory are documented in TESTING.md. devilfish707 compared the level fix with the JSFX on an Octatrack MKII and reported it working, then ran this build for about three minutes on seven tracks with p-lock automation and scenes. Browser packages and native parity proofs for 0.1.2 are pending.
gates: verify.py: reference error at two input levels, the AMP VOL level match, silence, COLOR and stereo isolation
benchmark.py: both cores, moving controls and all 16 trigger splits
Static worst-case cycle and exact memory accounting
Native/browser byte parity and placement/rejection checks (0.1.1; pending for 0.1.2)

conditions.parameterExtremes: DRIVE/TRIM endpoints and defaults, every COLOR, at -2 dBFS and at the unit's 0.22 FS working level: reference render; straight-line stereo loop costs 295 code cycles/sample at all settings.
conditions.parameterModulation: Both-core benchmark changes every active parameter at every 16-sample block; all 16 trigger splits. LFO, p-lock, CC and scene edits converge on these same parameter words. Hardware p-lock operation is author-reported.
conditions.modeSwitching: COLOR branch paths are bounded; two processing calls per block cover a trigger split, with reselection init charged separately. NONE bypass reduces work. Part/recovery behavior was not measured on hardware.
conditions.maxLoad: Eight inserts per core, FX1 and FX2 on each of four tracks, sixteen total. The static model includes control updates, a split and initialization; eight-FX2-instance render covers both cores. Standard dispatcher/streaming reserve is deducted from the core budget. Bus stalls are not measured.
conditions.inputConditions: Reference render covers silence, impulses, steps and 220 Hz–12 kHz tones. The sample loop and saturating stores contain no signal-dependent control transfers; full-scale input has the same instruction path.

regions.name: Program: 422 logical P words on each DSP core
Descriptor clone including its 14-byte stride padding

memory.conditions: Both-core logical allocation, including descriptor stride and COLOR formatter. Each 31-word state/scratch subset reuses an existing 256-word dispatcher block. No new Y buffer, heap, sample table, SDRAM or CPU RAM. Existing chooser/dispatcher scaffolding is accounted separately in evidence/memory.md; firmware storage packs DSP records into 3-byte words.

hardware.summary: On an Octatrack MKII the author flashed OCTABAM7 (this source), played about three minutes with TapeHead on seven tracks under parameter-lock automation and scene changes, and reported it sounds the same as OCTABAM6, which had been compared with the JSFX and reported working after 0.1.1 saturated less.
limitations: A listening report of about three minutes on seven tracks: not a measured hardware cycle, memory-canary, recording, recovery or maximum-load stress test.
Seven instances, not the sixteen-insert maximum the cycle model prices; no overload was reported, but none was measured either.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial: saturate a drum loop
steps: On a track playing a drum loop, hold FUNC and press FX2, turn LEVEL to TAPEHEAD and press YES. Press FX2 to see DRIVE 36, TRIM 18 and COLOR NORM.
Turn DRIVE to 100: the peaks flatten and the kick thickens. Turn TRIM to about 40 to bring the level down. Switch COLOR to BRGT for more top end, NORM for a darker tone.
Choose NONE in FX2 SETUP to compare with the dry track. Re-selecting TAPEHEAD clears its internal state.

access.location: FUNC + FX1 or FUNC + FX2 SETUP on an audio track: the effect chooser (LEVEL selects, YES assigns). DRIVE, TRIM and COLOR are on the FX main page.
steps: Select an audio track that plays a sample, transport stopped or running.
Hold FUNC and press FX2 (or FX1) to open its SETUP. Turn LEVEL to TAPEHEAD and press YES to assign it.
Press FX2 (or FX1) to show the main page: DRIVE, TRIM and COLOR. The SETUP page has no TapeHead controls.
The documented controls were captured on the emulator MKII panel; the author also reports working audio and parameter locks on an Octatrack of unspecified model.
